method.title: E. coli Transformation with Plasmid DNA (Heat Shock and Selective Plating)
method.summary: Competent E. coli cells are mixed with plasmid DNA by flicking, held briefly on ice, heat-shocked at 42°C, returned to ice, then spread onto an antibiotic-containing LB agar plate, which is inverted. Seven numbered steps, performed in order.

requirements.title: Add plasmid DNA to cells
requirements.description: Add 5 μL of plasmid DNA to the competent E. coli cells.
checks: Pipette is used to transfer liquid into the tube holding the competent cells
The tube receiving the DNA is the cell tube (typically kept in or taken from the green ice bucket)
This addition happens before any flicking, heat shock or plating
caveats: Volume of 5 μL cannot be verified from video
Identity of the plasmid DNA and of the competent E. coli cells depends on labels or contents not visible on camera
Competence of the cells and sterility cannot be confirmed

requirements.title: Flick tube to mix
requirements.description: Mix gently by flicking the tube 4-5 times.
checks: Operator flicks the tube with a finger rather than vortexing or pipetting up and down
Mixing occurs after the DNA has been added and before the tube goes back on ice
caveats: Exact count of 4-5 flicks may not be reliably countable on video
Whether the mixing is 'gentle' is a subjective judgement

requirements.title: Incubate mixture on ice
requirements.description: Incubate the DNA-cell mixture on ice for 5 seconds.
checks: Tube is placed into the ice in the green ice bucket
Tube is left in the ice for a period rather than moved on straight away
caveats: The duration of 5 seconds cannot be timed precisely from video
That the bucket contains ice at the correct cold temperature cannot be confirmed

requirements.title: Heat shock at 42°C
requirements.description: Rapidly transfer the tube to a pre-heated 42°C water bath for exactly 5 seconds.
checks: Tube is moved quickly from the ice to the heating apparatus
Tube is placed in the heating device (water bath per the procedure; the equipment list names a thermal cycler)
Tube stays in the heater briefly and is then removed
caveats: Temperature of 42°C and that the device was pre-heated cannot be verified on video
Exact 5-second duration cannot be confirmed precisely
The document is inconsistent: step 4 specifies a water bath but the equipment list says a thermal cycler is used for heat shock; either device may appear

requirements.title: Return tube to ice
requirements.description: Immediately return the tube to ice for 5 seconds.
checks: Tube goes back into the ice bucket directly after removal from the heater, with no intervening steps
Tube remains on ice for a period before plating
caveats: Duration of 5 seconds cannot be timed precisely
Ice temperature is not verifiable

requirements.title: Spread culture on LB plate
requirements.description: Spread 50μL of culture onto an LB agar plate containing the appropriate selective antibiotic.

Liquid is spread across the agar surface
Plating occurs after the final ice step
caveats: Volume of 50 μL cannot be verified from video
Presence and identity of the correct selective antibiotic in the plate depends on labels and is not visible

log: I should check key moments across the roughly 48-frame budget, mapping out the timeline: pipetting around 0-12s, flicking 12-30s, ice around 30-45s, thermal cycler 45-60s, more ice 60-70s, plating 67-110s. I want to verify the inversion step near 113s to see whether the plate is agar-side up.

Piecing together the sequence: the tube comes out of ice around 4.4, then pipetting happens into it while held by hand around 9-11, followed by placement in a rack by 13. Between 16-24 the hand seems to be touching or flicking the tube while it's in the rack, and by 32 there appears to be a second pipetting step into a tube held above the ice.

Around 36-44 the hand is holding a tube over the ice again, with the right hand flicking it using an index finger around 40-44. I want to look more closely at the 12-30 and 28-48 ranges to confirm these movements.

I'm piecing together the sequence: a tube was already in the rack from the start, then around 9-11 it's held in hand while being pipetted into, and by 13.3 the hand moves it back over the ice to return it.

Looking further, at 16-24 there's some touching at the rack that's ambiguous, then 29-32 shows another pipetting step with the tube held in the left hand above the ice — possibly the DNA addition step. Flicking happens with the right hand around 34-44, and by 46.8 the tube is carried to the thermal cycler as its lid opens. I'm noting the ice incubation step between flicking and heat shock may have been skipped, so I want to double-check the 44-47 window and the broader 47-70 range to confirm whether that step was actually performed.

I'm tracking the timeline: tube goes into ice at 60.4, pipette handling around 63-66, then retrieval at 68.6, placing step 5 within 59-68. Heat shock seems to occur 46-59 with the cycler lid opening and closing, followed by step 6 spanning roughly 68-106, and I need to verify step 7's inversion action using the remaining frames around 106-113.

I'm trying to figure out whether the plate is being inverted or flipped around the 109-111 mark, since the orientation is ambiguous from this angle. Looking at the plating sequence from 68-106, I notice the pipette dispensing liquid around 85 and 95-105, and at 88-92 the plate seems to be tilted and rotated rather than using a spreader tool — I'm trying to determine if this tilting motion counts as the spreading step.

For locating step 1, I'm comparing two possible DNA addition events: one around 9-11 where a tube is pulled from ice and pipetted, and another around 29-32 where pipetting happens above the ice. I'm trying to work out the sequence of which event represents the actual DNA addition versus just handling the tube before flicking occurs at 36-45.

For step 2's flicking check, I'm noting that the tube never returns to ice afterward — it goes straight to the cycler instead, which complicates whether the "mixing before returning to ice" check should be marked contradicted or not_visible, since the ice-return step seems absent entirely.

Step 3 (returning to ice) appears not_performed since the continuous footage shows the tube held and flicked over the ice bucket but then carried directly to the cycler, not placed back in. I also noticed an earlier moment around 13.3 where a hand passes over the ice before flicking, but that's before mixing occurs so it doesn't satisfy the method's required order.

For step 4, the cycler lid opens around 46-49, the tube placement itself isn't clearly visible, the lid closes around 50-55, then reopens at 57 and the tube comes out, going back toward ice around 60. On the "quickly" check, the tube seems to move from a hand positioned above the ice bucket rather than directly from the ice itself, so I'm leaning toward marking this as confirmed with a caveat noting it came from the hand rather than literally from the ice.

For step 5, spanning roughly 59-68, I'm confirming both that the tube gets placed in ice right after the cycler closes at 57.6, around 60.4, and that the tube stays in the ice from 60-68 while the pipette gets fetched. Step 6 covers the range from 68-106.

method.title: Passaging Adherent Cells in a 10 cm Dish Using Trypsin-EDTA in a Biosafety Cabinet
method.summary: The operator sanitises their hands and materials with 70% ethanol and moves a 10 cm dish of adherent cells from the incubator into the biosafety cabinet. They aspirate the medium, wash with PBS, and detach the cells with 0.25% Trypsin-EDTA. Complete medium is added to neutralise the trypsin, the cells are resuspended and transferred to a conical tube, and a portion is reseeded into a new 10 cm dish with fresh medium. The dish is rocked to spread the cells and returned to the incubator. Note that the document has internal inconsistencies: the tube size (15 ml vs 50 ml) and the reseeding volume (about 2 ml vs 5 ml).

I'm mapping out the key time windows with my limited frame budget, sketching the sequence from initial hand spraying through incubator removal, aspiration, PBS wash, trypsinization with the P1000 pipette, and medium addition, planning to cover roughly 48 frames across these stages.

I'll start with viewing 0-30 using 8 frames.
I'm tracking the spraying and aspiration steps around the dish, noting the pipette tilt and timing, then moving to the next phase of adding PBS and rocking before aspirating again.

I'm tracking the timeline: PBS gets drawn from the bottle and dispensed into the dish, followed by rocking and aspirating, then some hand tapping before moving into the trypsin step with the P1000, tilting and tapping the dish.

I'm tracking the sequence: trypsin added to the dish around 110-120s with tilting for distribution, then the operator grabs a tube from the bag with orange caps around 124-132s, followed by medium addition and pipetting from roughly 138-160s. With 16 frames remaining, I'm planning to sample segments around 136-172 and 172-212 to cover the rest of the sequence.

I'm piecing together the sequence of events around 140-215: drawing medium from a bottle, pipetting into a dish, then possibly transferring liquid to a conical tube with an orange cap, followed by work with a new dish and another pipetting step. I'm not fully certain when the transfer to the tube actually occurs within that window.

From the overview, I can place incubator and cleanup events later — around 226.8 the dish gets carried, 233.6 it's placed into the incubator, and from roughly 240-267 there's cleanup activity near a waste bin and cabinet, though the sash closure isn't clearly visible. I'll allocate the remaining frames to the 170-178 range to pin down the transfer step.

The transfer into the conical tube isn't clearly visible - around 168.5 the pipette lifts with liquid, and by 171 the dish looks mostly clear, with the operator handling a tube in the rack around 177. I'll mark this step as found but with low confidence, noting the dispensing action into the tube happened sometime in that window.

Moving on, the pause step before dispensing isn't clearly establishable either, so I'll mark it not visible. For the new dish appearing around 193 and the subsequent draws and pink liquid dispensing around 206-214, the source material is uncertain. The medium addition, rocking, and incubator placement steps around 220-233 are mostly unclear except for carrying and placing the dish, while door closing isn't visible and cleanup from 240-267 shows no sash.

Going back to the spraying step, around 9.4 there's a hand with a spray bottle near materials, followed by wiping with a paper towel at 16.9 and handling bottles at 20.6 - I'll mark this as found but partial. The earlier hand spraying and rubbing motions around 1.9-5.6 support the first step being found.

For gathering, I see bench activity from 16-28 with bottles carried to the hood at 28.1, which roughly confirms that step. The incubator opening sequence from 37-44 with a dish retrieved at 43.9 and the door closing confirms that step too.

Following the dish through the process: it's carried into the cabinet at 48.3 and placed on the surface at 57.1, where the aspirator appears in hand and aspiration occurs with the dish tilted. The tilting continues at the edge, then PBS is drawn from the labeled bottle around 80.8 with the pipette positioned over the dish at 84.3.

Rocking motion appears moderate at 87.8, followed by aspiration again at 91.3 and P1000 pipette use into the dish from 106.6-110.9.
